$comment: Generated from the xeo-*.ttl modules by tools/gen_profile.py — do not edit by hand.

conventions.label: the class local name, PascalCase
conventions.propertyKey: the datatype property local name, camelCase
conventions.relationshipType: UPPER_SNAKE of the object property local name

AlgorithmRun.definition: One execution of one algorithm over one projection of the graph at a time: immutable once finished. Carries algorithm (which method), parameters (as run), projection (what it ran on) and ranAt. The provenance record for every score and derived edge it wrote: outputs point back with computedBy, or name the run in their method. Re-running with a different projection or parameters is a new run, never an update to an old one.

AnswerEngine.definition: An assistant that answers a person in its own interface, with or without web search and citations: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and multi-turn agents and voice surfaces acting for a user (ConversationalAgent until 0.7). The AEO surface.

AttributedCredit.definition: One touch's credit for one conversion under one model: creditedTouchpoint, creditFor, usesAttributionModel, creditShare, and attributedRevenue and attributedConversions where they apply. The credits of one conversion under one model sum to 1 (or, for full_credit_each, each is 1).

AttributionModel.definition: A rule for giving conversions' credit to touches, described by its structure, not its name: creditRule, its CreditAnchors (positions and weights), lookbackWindow, the touch types eligible, deduplicationRule, dateBasis and revenueBasis. Vendor names such as 'U-shaped' are mapped in mappings/, not trusted: two vendors' U-shaped can put the remaining credit on different touches. A rule, so a norm; a changed rule is a new AttributionModel.

AttributionRollup.definition: Credited totals for one channel, campaign, ad set or ad over one window under one model: attributedRevenue and attributedConversions, with periodStart, periodEnd, usesAttributionModel and method. A MetricReading of an attribution Metric. The graph keeps rollups; the per-touch credits may live in the column store.

BookedMeeting.definition: A meeting booked through a scheduler or by a salesperson: a kind of ConversionEvent. Its outcome (held, no-show) is callOutcome.

Brand.definition: A named market identity that engines may mention, cite, or recommend. Distinct from Website: a brand can be visible on the whole web, not only its own origin.

Call.definition: A phone call that happened: a kind of ConversionEvent, captured by a call-tracking system. Carries occurredAt and, once judged, callOutcome.

Campaign.definition: A body of work inside a Project against one Topic: the URLs and Terms it covers, and the single Objective it is measured by. Recommendations are issuedFor a campaign, and it is the unit an operator plans a cycle around. Soft-deleted like its Project.

Capability.definition: A lever or strength a party can bring to bear (content, technical, PR, brand, ...). The unit of the scope gate: a Tactic is in reach only when every Capability it requires is approved. Specific capabilities are instances, not subclasses.

Chargeback.definition: A payment reversed by the buyer's bank against an Order (refundsOrder). Carries refundedAmount. Its grounding is provisional: chargeback records differ most between processors.

Consent.definition: One recorded consent choice, for one purpose (consentPurpose), by one subject (consentSubject), as one system captured it (consentCapturedBy), with its status and when it was recorded. A new choice is a new Consent, never an edit; the current status for a subject and purpose is the latest. Company-level choices, such as not using a company's data to train models, sit on the Organization. Validity under any law is an interpretation made elsewhere, not part of this record.

ConversionEvent.definition: A submission/click/unlock that happened at a time: a visitor's action on a ConversionPoint, recorded by the capturing system. Immutable once recorded. Identified by the capturing system and its submission id; one per submission. Not the creation of a CRM record, which may follow, be merged into an existing record, or never happen: events are not leads.

ConversionPoint.definition: A durable on-page mechanism that turns attention into a pipeline event. Identified by the URL it sits on and its form id or selector. Its kind is conversionPointType.

Crawl.definition: One crawl run over one Website: time-bounded, agent-attributed, immutable once finished.

CreditAnchor.definition: One fixed position a position-based model gives a share to, and the share: anchorPosition and anchorWeight. A U-shaped model has two (first_touch 0.4, lead_created 0.4); the rest is spread by the model's rule.

Diagnostic.definition: A named, reusable check or framework that reads observations and reveals gaps (e.g. a waterfall-position assessment). The framework is durable; each finding it produces is a Gap.

DiagnosticRun.definition: One execution of a Diagnostic against one scope at a time: immutable once finished, method-attributed. The Diagnostic is the durable check; the run is the occasion it was applied, and each Gap it found is revealedIn that run. Carries ranAt and websiteId. A later run supersedes an earlier one without deleting it, so a finding can always be traced to the data it was read from.

Domain.definition: A registrable domain (the public suffix plus one label, e.g. example.co.uk), identified by its name in lower case. The publisher-level identity a URL sits on, whether or not the site is under observation: a competitor's result has no partOf edge to a tracked Website, it has onDomain. Not tenant-scoped: one node per domain, shared by every tenant that sees it, and it carries no websiteId.

Engine.definition: A system that mediates between a person's question and web content. A parent class only: every engine node is one of its subtypes, SearchEngine (here), or GenerativeOverview or AnswerEngine (visibility).

Entity.definition: A real-world thing or concept that content is about — a product, a place, a person, a material, a method — identified by a reference into a public knowledge base (entityRef) where one exists, otherwise by name. Distinct from Topic, which is a site-scoped grouping somebody derived, and from Brand, which is a market identity engines mention: an Entity is the thing itself, shared across sites. Not tenant-scoped. Named for the knowledge-graph sense of the word; not to be confused with the layer 'entity', which Website, URL and Term also occupy.

Experiment.definition: A test of a tactic that ran over a time window: immutable once concluded, method-attributed. The precedent record the decision layer learns from.

ExternalEvent.definition: Something outside the work that happened at a time and could move the metrics an experiment reads: an engine's ranking update, a site migration, an outage, a seasonal peak, a competitor's launch. Carries name and occurredAt. An episode, recorded once and shared: whether it actually affected a given result is a separate claim, carried on confoundedBy.

Feedback.definition: An operator's judgment of a machine's claim, hung off whatever it judges (feedbackOn): a diagnosed Gap, or the Recommendation issued to close one. Carries a verdict (a slotted-in concept), a statement in the operator's words, and who gave it and when. Not a TacticAssessment, which is a scored estimate of an approach on one dimension: Feedback is a person agreeing or disagreeing with a claim about one case. Never deleted: a rejected finding and the reason it was rejected are what a learned Practice is later drawn from.

Framework.definition: A named method: a set of Stages, ordered or not, with the Diagnostics, Tactics and Practices hung on them. An optimization waterfall (ordered stages, each with a test, a subject placed at the first stage it fails), a tactic matrix, a launch checklist and a discipline playbook are all Frameworks, told apart by frameworkKind and never by subclass. A norm: it says how the work should be approached, it is authored and revisable, and it is identified by name within its author's scope. Distinct from Playbook, which is the unordered bundle a discipline reuses; a Framework adds the structure, and may include what a Playbook includes. The method is the instance you author. XEO ships the frame and none of the stages.

Gap.definition: A diagnosed deficit between current and desired visibility. First-order, but a claim: asserted by a Diagnostic from evidence, never observed directly. Its kind (gapType) is a slotted-in skos:Concept — e.g. a Citation-Waterfall stage — not a subclass baked into the ontology.

GenerativeOverview.definition: A search engine's generated answer on its own results page: Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, Bing's generated answers. Tied to the SearchEngine it appears on (shownOnSearchEngine). The GEO surface. Was GenerativeEngine until 0.7.

IdentityLink.definition: The claim that an identifier (a cookie id, a device id, an email hash, a click id, an IP address) belongs to a Person or Organization. Carries linkedIdentifier, identityResolvesTo, identityMethod and confidence. A derivation, because two resolvers can link the same identifier differently.

InboundReference.definition: A page on another site that links to or mentions you: your URL, Website, Brand or Organization. Observed, however it came about. Carries referencingUrl (the page), referenceTarget (what it points at or names), referenceKind (link or mention), and firstSeenAt and lastSeenAt; anchorText where it is a link. How it came about is not part of it: a placement, a pitch or a link magnet is a Tactic, linked from decision with acquiredByTactic, and an organic reference has none. A link between two pages of sites you crawl is linksTo; this is the record of a reference to you, kept whether or not you crawl the other site.

Intervention.definition: A category of tactic in a controlled vocabulary you bring. A skos:Concept, so a whole intervention taxonomy slots in without touching the ontology.

Journey.definition: The ordered Touchpoints of one Person or Organization (journeyOf) leading to their conversions. A derivation: stitching touches to one party is a resolution, so it carries method, and the IdentityLinks it used. Account-level journeys (an Organization's) and person-level ones are both journeys.

LLMResponse.definition: One captured response from one engine/model for one Prompt at a moment: time-bounded, source-attributed, immutable once captured. The visibility sibling of SerpSnapshot.

Metric.definition: A named, reusable definition of a measured quantity: what is counted or computed, over which records, aggregated how, in what unit, and which way is better. A rule, not a number: the number is a MetricReading. One node per definition, identified by its skos:notation within its scheme (xeos:metric is the published reference scheme). Two Metrics are the same when metricType, aggregation, readsSlot or inputs, metricFilter, timeAnchor and unit all match; changing any of them makes a new Metric, never an edit, because readings and targets are anchored to the definition. Carries exactly one metricType, unit, betterDirection and additivity. A simple metric also carries aggregation and readsSlot; a ratio carries numerator and denominator and has unit ratio; a derived metric carries expression and at least one inputMetric. A skos:Concept, so a consumer adds its own metrics as instances without touching the ontology.

MetricReading.definition: The value one Metric took over one window, for one scope, from one source. One row per metric, scope, window and source: its identity is readingOf, scope, periodStart, periodEnd, source and, where the source deduplicates in more than one way, aggregationBasis. Requires value, periodStart, periodEnd and readingOf, and should carry websiteId and datasetUri; a ratio reading also carries numeratorValue and denominatorValue. An observation only when the primary API returned exactly that metric, window and scope. When the value was rolled up, recomputed, or taken from a vendor's model, the reading is a derivation and carries method and confidence. High-cardinality readings live in the column store; the graph holds the windowed readings a target, an Outcome or an Objective points at.

MetricTarget.definition: One measurable target of an Objective: the Metric it is set on (targetMetric, a link to the Metric node), the targetValue to reach, read per targetKind as an absolute value or as a change from a captured baseline (baselineReading), and whether it isPrimary. Unit and better direction come from its Metric. Named a target and never a key result: xeo:Outcome is 'the measured result an experiment produced', an observation, and a goal must not share a name with a reading. Each target is its own node so the experiment loop can hang observations off it; a target dropped on edit is stamped deletedAt, never destroyed, because its id is what measured history is anchored to.

Model.definition: A machine-learning model as a durable thing: one node per build (claude-opus-5-5 as of a given date, a BERT checkpoint, a ranking model). Carries modelFamily, modelVersion and modelKind; optionally its architecture, size and where it runs. An AI answer or a model call points at the Model that produced it with producedByModel. Distinct from the plain model text field, which only names one.

Objective.definition: What a Campaign intends to move: an operator-written statement in prose (carried verbatim — the recommendation agent reads it as the goal), a resultsWindowDays every target is measured over, and one or more MetricTargets of which exactly one isPrimary. An intent set at creation. A campaign has one reporting horizon, distinct from the Project's work window: a two-month engagement can carry a six-month results window. The window starts on resultsWindowStart, and the objective-level result is one objectiveReading per target over the campaign's deduplicated scope, never a sum of Outcomes.

Order.definition: A purchase placed: what was bought, for how much, before payment settles. Carries grossAmount, discountAmount, taxAmount, shippingAmount and, once paid, paidAmount.

Organization.definition: The canonical organization: one node per real organization (an agency, a brand's company, an in-house team, a customer's company), which every system's record of it (a CRM company, an ad account's owner, a billing customer) points at with refersTo. Identified by name. The owner of Websites and Brands (owns), the holder of Capabilities and the client of another Organization (holdsCapability and clientOf, in xeo-work), and a tenancy node that activates Frameworks and Playbooks. It copies no vendor's fields: what a CRM knows about the company stays on the CRM's record, which refers to this node. Its kind is a slotted-in concept (organizationKind), never a subclass.

Outcome.definition: The measured result an experiment produced: the comparison of a resultReading against a baselineReading of one Metric over one scope, recorded as absoluteChange, relativeChange and result. The measurement is an observation; any claim that the tactic CAUSED it is an interpretation, carried on the Recommendation, not asserted here.

OwnerChange.definition: A CRM record being reassigned from one owner to another: happened at a time, immutable once recorded. Carries crmRecordRef, ownerRef (the owner it was assigned to), occurredAt, and method saying how the row was obtained, as on a StageTransition. One row per reassignment. Read from the CRM's history, so every CRM can fill it and none states it as a field.

Payment.definition: Money received against an Order or a Subscription. Carries paidAmount.

Person.definition: The canonical person: one node per real person (a contact, a lead, a known visitor, a client's marketer, a team member), which every system's record of that person (a HubSpot contact, a Hyros lead, a SegMetrics visitor) points at with refersTo, so all of a person's representations join the same way. Its identity is a key the implementation mints; an email or a name is how a record is matched to it, not what it is. It copies no vendor's fields: a lifecycle stage, an owner or a source channel stays on the system's record that refers to it.

PipelineRollup.definition: A MetricReading of a pipeline Metric (leads_created, pipeline_created, deals_won, revenue_won, ...) for one website over one window, computed from CRM records. Always a derivation: the records are observed, the windowed number is XEO's computation over them, so it carries method. Requires what any reading does (readingOf, value, periodStart, periodEnd) with datasetUri pointing at the authoritative table, and currencyCode when its Metric's unit is currency. The graph keeps this rollup; the rows it was computed from stay in the column store.

Playbook.definition: A reusable, discipline-scoped bundle of Diagnostics, Tactics, and Practices — an 'SEO playbook', an 'AEO playbook', a 'local playbook'. Durable and named, like a Diagnostic. Its scope is the DISCIPLINE, not the account: a Playbook is authored once (by the community or an agency) and reused across every client. What varies per client or campaign is which Playbooks a tenancy activates and which Practices it overrides — never the Playbook itself.

Practice.definition: A standing rule that governs how recommendations are made under stated conditions. Best-practices, SOPs, and lessons-learned are all Practices, distinguished by source, not by class. A Practice does one of three things (practiceKind): veto a candidate (guardrail), reorder it (preference), or attach a caveat (guidance). Revisable and versioned (supersedes); scoped to the concepts it appliesToConcept; audited on the recommendations it fired on (appliedPractice).

Project.definition: The contractual container for a body of work on one Website. Declares its engagementType (retainer or one-off), an interventionQuota (a scope of work with no ceiling is not a scope), a cadence the quota resets over (retainer) or a durationDays it runs for (one-off), and the Interventions and Tactics inScope under the contract. Never destroyed: its campaigns, objectives and targets are the substrate the end-of-campaign report and the experiment loop read, so it is stamped deletedAt and filtered, not deleted.

Prompt.definition: A tracked natural-language question posed to engines. Distinct from Term: a prompt is what a person asks; the engine's retrieval fans out into Terms.

Recommendation.definition: The labeled claim the whole chain exists to produce: deploy this Tactic to close this Gap, supported by these Experiments, at a given priority. An interpretation — carries method, confidence, and who/what issued it.

Refund.definition: Money returned to the buyer against an Order (refundsOrder). Carries refundedAmount.

RevenueEvent.definition: Money moving at a time, recorded by a store or a payment processor: the parent of Order, Payment, Refund and Chargeback. Immutable once recorded. Carries occurredAt, currencyCode, the amounts that apply, revenueSubject and, where known, customerStatus.

SearchIntent.definition: Why the person is asking. Modeled as named individuals, not free strings. Since 0.6.0 the same four values are also published as concepts in xeos:searchIntent, each a SearchIntent, which is the form to write.

SearchPerformanceFact.definition: The atomic ground-truth metric row for one (websiteId, address, term, date [, device, country]) tuple. Never instantiated as graph relationships; the graph carries windowed ranksFor rollups whose datasetUri points back to the authoritative table.

SerpSnapshot.definition: One observation of a search results page for a Term at a moment, for a stated engine, locale, and device.

SpendRollup.definition: What an ad platform reports for one campaign, ad set or ad (spendLevel and its pointer) over one window: spendAmount in currencyCode, impressions and clicks, with periodStart, periodEnd and source. The column store keeps the daily rows; the graph keeps windowed rollups.

Stage.definition: One step or cell of a Framework: a named position that Diagnostics, Tactics and Gaps are placed at (atStage). Carries name, an optional stageOrder, and an optional test — the question a subject must pass to move on. Belongs to exactly one Framework (hasStage) and is identified by name within it. In an ordered Framework, nextStage links each stage to the one after.

StageTransition.definition: A CRM record entering a stage: happened at a time, immutable once recorded. Identified by crmRecordRef, stageSlot, toStageRef and enteredAt. One row per entry, and a record that returns to a stage enters it again as a new row. Carries fromStageRef where the previous stage is known, exitedAt once it has left, amountAtTransition, datasetUri, and method saying how the row was obtained: vendor-history (the CRM's own history rows), vendor-calculated-property (a per-stage entry timestamp the CRM maintains), or snapshot-diff (two reads compared). High-cardinality, so it lives in the column store and the graph holds rollups. A calculated property that is cleared when a record moves backwards, or filled when it skips a stage, is not a record of what happened and never fills this.

Subscription.definition: An agreement to pay a recurringValue every billing period (billingInterval and billingIntervalCount), from a start date until cancelled. Its Payments are RevenueEvents.

Tactic.definition: A durable, named approach that can address gaps. Categorized by a slotted-in intervention taxonomy (inIntervention), scored on slotted-in dimensions (assessedAs -> TacticAssessment), and gated by the Capabilities it requires.

TacticAssessment.definition: A scored estimate of a tactic on ONE dimension (onDimension), carrying score, method, and confidence. The dimension set (impact / risk / time-to-value, or ICE, or your own) and how dimensions are weighted are a strategy-layer concern; this class only records that an assessment was made, on what dimension, and by what method.

Term.definition: A search query string, unique by name. Data sources are attributed on observations that mention the term, never as subtypes of the term.

Topic.definition: A named grouping of Terms and/or URLs produced by a clustering or labeling process. Site-scoped. Assignments (inTopic for a Term, about for a URL or Prompt) carry method, model, and confidence.

Touchpoint.definition: One interaction a person or organization had with your marketing at a time: an ad click or view, a visit, an email or an email open, a text message, a call, a form, a meeting. Immutable once recorded. Carries touchType, occurredAt, touchChannel, and what the source gives: the UTM fields, clickIdentifier, adCampaignRef, adSetRef, adRef, referringPlatform, touchLandingUrl. Belongs to a Journey.

URL.definition: A resource address within a Website. Durable identity; the state of the resource at a time is recorded by Fetch observations.

Website.definition: A site under observation, identified by its origin. The tenancy scope for URLs, crawls, and topics.
